cls: Sclerosing agent (detergent-type) for varicose veins / spider veins
pharm: Detergent sclerosant that, on intravenous injection into varicose or telangiectatic veins, damages the vascular endothelium and induces localized fibrosis and vessel occlusion, obliterating the treated vein; also has local anesthetic properties.
quick: 0.5% for spider veins, 1% for reticular veins; ~0.1-0.3 mL per injection, max ~10 mL/session
Caution; discard milk for ~2-3 days after treatment if used
No specific adjustment; use with caution
No specific adjustment; use with caution
Injection-site reactions, allergic/anaphylactic reactions, signs of DVT/PE, visual symptoms
summary: Polidocanol is a detergent-type sclerosing agent injected directly into incompetent superficial veins to treat uncomplicated spider veins (very small varicose veins, <=1 mm) and uncomplicated small varicose (reticular) veins (1-3 mm) of the lower extremities. After intravenous injection it disrupts the endothelial lining of the vein, exposing subendothelial collagen and causing localized thrombosis, inflammation, and ultimately fibrotic obliteration (sclerosis) of the treated vessel, which is then reabsorbed and fades from view. It is supplied as a 0.5% solution for spider veins and a 1% solution for reticular veins, and is also used as a foam (mixed with air/gas) for larger veins in some settings. It must be administered by a physician trained in venous procedures, using the smallest effective volume. The main risks are local injection-site reactions and, less commonly, serious adverse events including deep vein thrombosis, pulmonary embolism, arterial embolism, severe allergic/anaphylactic reactions, tissue necrosis from extravasation or intra-arterial injection, and transient visual disturbances. It also has weak local anesthetic action.
indications: Treatment of uncomplicated spider veins (varicose veins <=1 mm in diameter) of the lower extremities
Treatment of uncomplicated reticular veins (small varicose veins 1 to 3 mm in diameter) of the lower extremities

dosage.n: Use the lowest effective concentration/volume; repeat sessions as needed at intervals
Smaller veins respond to lower concentrations

dosage.d: Do not exceed approximately 10 mL of solution per treatment session
dosage.n: Limit total dose to reduce systemic and thrombotic risk

admin: Administer only by a physician trained and experienced in venous anatomy, diagnosis, and treatment of vein conditions, with resuscitation equipment available
Inject slowly intravenously into the target vein using the lowest effective volume and concentration; aspirate to confirm intravenous placement and avoid intra-arterial injection
Avoid extravasation, which can cause local tissue necrosis; if it occurs, manage the injection site appropriately
Apply compression (stockings/bandage) after treatment and encourage ambulation to reduce thrombotic risk, per protocol
Inspect the solution for particulate matter/discoloration before use; do not mix with other agents
moa: Polidocanol is a nonionic detergent sclerosant. When injected intravascularly, its amphiphilic structure interacts with and disrupts the lipid bilayer of vascular endothelial cells, denaturing surface proteins and destroying the endothelium of the targeted vein. This endothelial injury exposes the subendothelial collagen, triggers localized platelet activation, thrombosis, and an inflammatory reaction within the vessel wall. The treated vein then undergoes fibrosis and is converted into a fibrous cord (sclerosis) that is gradually reabsorbed, eliminating the abnormal vein. By concentrating the detergent effect within the targeted vessel and using minimal volumes, surrounding tissues are spared. Polidocanol additionally has local anesthetic properties, which reduce injection discomfort.

absolute: Acute thromboembolic disease (e.g., acute deep vein thrombosis or pulmonary embolism)
relative: Known right-to-left cardiac shunt (e.g., symptomatic patent foramen ovale) - increased risk with foam sclerotherapy
Significant peripheral arterial disease or immobility
History of thrombophilia or prior venous thromboembolism
Acute systemic illness or local infection at the treatment site
monitor: Injection-site reactions, including hyperpigmentation, necrosis, and ulceration
Allergic and anaphylactic reactions during and after injection
Signs and symptoms of deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism
Neurologic and visual symptoms (especially with foam)
Arterial complications if inadvertent intra-arterial injection occurs

preg: There are no adequate data on polidocanol use in pregnant women; treatment of varicose/spider veins is elective and should be deferred. Avoid use during pregnancy. Many such veins also improve after pregnancy, supporting postponement of treatment.
lact: It is not known whether polidocanol is excreted in human milk. As a precaution, breastfeeding should be interrupted for a period (commonly about 2-3 days) after treatment, or treatment deferred, weighing the elective nature of the procedure against any potential risk to the infant.
renal: No specific renal dose adjustment is described; polidocanol is used in small intravascular amounts. Use with general caution and standard precautions in patients with renal impairment.
hepatic: No specific hepatic dose adjustment is described. Use with general caution in patients with hepatic impairment, applying the lowest effective volume and concentration.

major: No clinically significant systemic drug interactions are established for the small intravascular doses used
moderate: Combined oral contraceptives and hormone replacement therapy - may add to venous thromboembolic risk; consider in patients with thrombotic risk factors
Anticoagulants/antiplatelet agents - theoretical influence on local thrombotic response and bruising
minor: Heparin/other agents are not routinely combined with the injectate
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction with alcohol is described.
interactions.diagnostics: No routine laboratory monitoring is required; duplex ultrasound may be used to assess veins and to exclude deep venous involvement before treatment.

common: Injection-site reactions - pain, bruising, irritation, warmth, swelling
Injection-site hyperpigmentation (brown discoloration along the vein)
Localized thrombosis in the treated vein (intravascular coagulum)
Pruritus or redness at the site
serious: Deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism
Tissue necrosis or ulceration (extravasation or inadvertent intra-arterial injection)
Arterial embolism / stroke-like events (rare, more with foam)
Visual disturbances and migraine-like symptoms (with foam)
rare: Nerve injury at the injection site
Embolic events through a right-to-left shunt
emergency: Sudden shortness of breath or chest pain (pulmonary embolism)
Leg swelling, pain, and warmth (deep vein thrombosis)
Severe allergic reaction (difficulty breathing, swelling, hives, collapse)
Sudden visual loss, weakness, or speech difficulty (embolic/neurologic event)
Severe injection-site pain with skin changes (necrosis/intra-arterial injection)

monitoring: Observe the patient during and after injection for hypersensitivity/anaphylactic reactions
Inspect injection sites for necrosis, ulceration, and hyperpigmentation, and treat localized intravascular thrombi as needed
Monitor for signs and symptoms of deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism, particularly with larger volumes or foam
Watch for neurologic or visual symptoms, especially when foam is used and in patients with a possible right-to-left shunt
Apply and review post-procedure compression and encourage ambulation
counsel: This treatment is injected into your problem veins by a trained doctor to close them off so they gradually fade
Bruising, brown discoloration, mild swelling, or firmness along the vein is common and usually settles over weeks to months
Wear the compression stockings as instructed and keep walking/moving to lower the small risk of blood clots
Seek urgent care for sudden shortness of breath, chest pain, or a painful, swollen, warm leg (possible clot)
Get emergency help for any difficulty breathing, swelling, or widespread rash (allergic reaction), or for sudden vision or speech problems
Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, breastfeeding, take hormone therapy/birth control, or have a history of blood clots
pk: Endothelial damage occurs immediately on contact; visible vein fading over weeks
Local sclerosing effect develops over days as thrombosis/fibrosis sets in
Local action; systemic levels from the small dose are low and rapidly cleared
Treated vein is permanently obliterated and reabsorbed; cosmetic result evolves over weeks to months
Store at controlled room temperature; do not freeze; inspect before use per label
pearls: Detergent sclerosant for SMALL superficial veins - 0.5% for spider veins (<=1 mm) and 1% for reticular veins (1-3 mm); always use the smallest effective volume (limit ~10 mL/session)
Must be given by a physician trained in venous procedures - confirm intravenous (not intra-arterial) placement; inadvertent intra-arterial injection can cause severe tissue necrosis
Foam (air/gas-mixed) formulations are used for larger veins and carry a greater risk of DVT/PE, visual disturbances, and embolic events - especially in patients with a right-to-left cardiac shunt
Post-treatment compression and early ambulation reduce thromboembolic risk; hyperpigmentation along the vein is common but usually temporary
Polidocanol also has a local anesthetic effect, easing injection discomfort
Avoid in pregnancy (treatment is elective) and in acute thromboembolic disease
missed: Not applicable. Polidocanol is administered during in-office treatment sessions by a physician, not on a patient-managed dosing schedule, so there is no missed-dose scenario; further sessions are scheduled by the treating clinician.
overdose: Excessive volume or concentration increases the risk of local tissue necrosis and of systemic and thromboembolic complications. There is no specific antidote. Management is supportive: monitor for and treat allergic reactions, local necrosis, and signs of deep vein thrombosis or pulmonary embolism, and provide appropriate wound, anticoagulant, and supportive care as indicated.
